title: Vietnamese Prawn Summer Rolls with Peanut Dip
summary: Fresh Vietnamese-style summer rolls filled with prawns, rice noodles, crunchy vegetables and herbs, served with a creamy peanut, lime and tamari dip. They make a light, refreshing pescatarian lunch for warm days.

ingredients.name: warm vegetable stock for loosening the dip

steps: Cook the rice noodles according to the packet instructions until tender, usually 3–5 minutes. Drain, rinse under cold water, and shake dry so they do not make the rolls soggy.
Prepare the fillings: halve the prawns lengthways, shred the lettuce, cut the cucumber and carrot into thin matchsticks, pick the herb leaves, and slice the spring onions.

Make the peanut dip by whisking together the peanut butter, tamari, lime juice, maple syrup, sesame oil, ginger, garlic and sriracha. Whisk in the warm vegetable stock a little at a time until the sauce is smooth, glossy and spoonable.
Set up a rolling station with a shallow dish of warm water and a clean damp board or tea towel. Soften one rice paper wrapper in the water for about 10–15 seconds until pliable but not floppy.

Lay the wrapper flat. Add a small strip of lettuce, noodles, cucumber, carrot, herbs and spring onion across the lower third, then place a few prawn halves just above the vegetables with the cut side facing up.
Fold the bottom of the wrapper over the filling, fold in the sides, then roll up firmly but gently to seal. The roll should feel snug and hold together without tearing.
Repeat with the remaining wrappers and filling. Keep finished rolls under a lightly damp tea towel so they stay soft.
Serve the summer rolls whole or halved, with the peanut dip on the side.
